assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led from peptide biology and incretin action to widely used therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with very large clinical and public-health impact; the chain from basic discovery to transformative medicine is clear and still expanding.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology and gut-hormone physiology), Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action) and Knudsen (long-acting analogue development) span physiology to drug design. Mojsov's sequence and activity work is also credited and the supplied credit exceeds three, so some allocation is unavoidably contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation across basic, clinical and outcome trials; timing is strong given the recent therapeutic impact.
uncertainties: Allocation among four credited people, with a contested priority claim on the original peptide work, is unresolved.
Long-term safety and outcome data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality; the concept and clinical proof are clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation costimulated CARs), June (clinical translation to CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, early CAR and TIL trials) form a plausible trio; earlier CAR concept work by others (e.g. Eshhar) is not in the supplied credit, which I cannot assess.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up; expansion to solid tumours remains limited, but the haematological proof is firm.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should include other early CAR pioneers outside the supplied list.
Toxicity and limits in solid tumours.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling, with IRE1/HAC1/XBP1 splicing as a mechanistic cornerstone and wide relevance to proteostasis, secretory physiology, metabolism, cancer and neurodegeneration.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the natural pair for the core mechanism of ER-stress signalling; the supplied credit supports a clean two-person configuration, though I am unsure whether other contributors (e.g. Kaufman, Ron) are credited elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed repeatedly over three decades and is textbook knowledge; recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is still early, so the prize case rests mainly on basic-science impact.
Credit of related contributors outside this candidate is not assessable here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of BCR-ABL by imatinib converted chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal to a chronic disease and established the template of molecularly targeted cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery programme), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) fit exactly three; the fair weighting of Sawyers' resistance work against the original drug discovery is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data and many successor kinase inhibitors; the discovery is fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Upstream credit for BCR-ABL discovery (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore and others) may overlap with prior recognition and is not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identified a central nutrient-sensing controller of growth and metabolism, with consequences for ageing, cancer, diabetes and immunosuppression; the concept is original and has reshaped cell physiology.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR and its role in growth control; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and key complexes. Schreiber's rapamycin chemical-biology work is important but I would leave him out for a two-person prize; this is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed; clinical impact via rapalogs is real but moderate, and the biology is mature.
uncertainties: Role of Schreiber and of others who identified mTOR (Sabatini, Brown, Sabers) is a close allocation question.
Recent controversies around one candidate may affect the committee's view; I cannot verify them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, linking pathogen sensing, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and anti-tumour immunity; a clear, original pathway with strong mechanistic grounding.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING. This pair covers the decisive steps, while other credited names (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) are important co-discoverers whose contributions overlap.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed; therapeutic translation (agonists, antagonists) is not yet established, which makes timing somewhat early.
uncertainties: Dispute over who made the decisive contributions, and the exclusion of other credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a transformative tool for causal control of defined cell populations, with broad use in neuroscience and some translational examples; the discovery and the tool development are both original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Microbial rhodopsin channel discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenböck) are separate steps; six credited names exceed the three-person limit and any trio leaves out decisive contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully adopted across labs; clinical application is still emerging, so the case is chiefly as a tool.
uncertainties: Severe allocation problem across six credited people.
A methods prize relative to a disease-mechanism discovery may be weighed differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a clear mechanism-to-medicine story with dramatic clinical effect.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are a coherent pair; contributions from SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) are not in the supplied credit and cannot be assessed.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up; the concept generalises to other antisense drugs but the discovery is narrower than broader platform candidates.
uncertainties: Credit for upstream SMN gene identification is not within the supplied names.
Narrower field impact than platform-level candidates.
